2_Introduction: The PSCs achieved a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.1099%, with VOC of 1.1704 V, FF of 81.1121%, and JSC of 26.45 mA/cm². The Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 (1.65 mol/L) perovskite precursor solution was prepared. The perovskite was deposited via a two-step spin-coating procedure with 1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s. 150 µL of antisolvent was dripped on the spinning substrate at the last 15 s of the second spin-coating step. The sample was then annealed at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The achieved high performance originates from precise crystallization control of the triple-cation Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3 perovskite, where the synergistic A-site cation mixture, with small-radius Cs⁺ improving thermal stability and the FA⁺/MA⁺ pair optimizing the tolerance factor, suppresses undesirable phase segregation and mitigates ion migration tendencies. The employed two-step spin-coating procedure, utilizing a relatively high precursor concentration (1.65 mol/L), first ensures uniform solution spreading at 1000 rpm before a rapid transition to 5500 rpm, which induces strong centrifugal force to thin the film and initiate dense packing of nuclei; the critical timing of the 150 µL antisolvent drip at the final 15 seconds then triggers a controlled, rapid supersaturation, promoting a high-density, homogeneous nucleation event that templates the subsequent growth of large, vertically aligned grains during the 110°C anneal. This optimized crystallization kinetics minimizes the formation of intra-grain and grain boundary defects, such as Pb⁰ and I⁻ vacancies, while the completed anneal eliminates residual solvent and intermediate phases, resulting in a dense, pinhole-free morphology with enhanced structural order that facilitates efficient charge transport and extraction by suppressing non-radiative recombination pathways, ultimately yielding a champion device with a VOC of 1.1704 V, JSC of 26.45 mA/cm², FF of 81.1121%, and a PCE of 25.1099%.
